evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/push_fanout.rs:367-376 — `send_fcm` (FCM HTTP v1) only flags a device token for eviction when the upstream error status matches `"NOT_REGISTERED" | "UNREGISTERED" | "INVALID_REGISTRATION"`. The FCM v1 status `"INVALID_ARGUMENT"` (HTTP 400, returned for a permanently malformed/garbage registration token) and `"NOT_FOUND"` (HTTP 404) are NOT in the match, so the function returns `(false, false)` — send failed, token NOT expired.

The second bool of the returned tuple is the 'evict this token' signal (the caller deletes the stored token only when it is true — see the APNs sibling at push_fanout.rs:844-959 which evicts on BadDeviceToken/Unregistered). A token that FCM rejects as INVALID_ARGUMENT is therefore never pruned from storage and is re-attempted on every subsequent fanout, producing a permanent per-fanout failed-send + warn log for that device with no self-healing.

The legacy path `send_fcm_legacy` (push_fanout.rs:449-456) has the same shape: it evicts only on `"NotRegistered" | "InvalidRegistration"` and would likewise retain a token FCM rejects for other permanent reasons.

Fix: treat FCM v1 `INVALID_ARGUMENT`/`NOT_FOUND` (and HTTP 400/404 with a token-scoped error) as evict-worthy, i.e. add them to the `expired` match so a permanently invalid token is pruned rather than retried forever. Confirm against the current FCM v1 error-code table before finalizing which codes are token-permanent vs message-level.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/push_fanout.rs:280 — `.expect("reqwest client build should not fail")` and push_fanout.rs:773 — `.expect("reqwest APNs client build should not fail")`. `reqwest::ClientBuilder::build()` is fallible at runtime (it can error on TLS-backend / native-cert-store initialization, not just on programmer misconfiguration), so these are runtime panics living inside the notification-fanout service rather than compile-time invariants.

A panic here aborts the calling task/worker on the push path instead of degrading gracefully (skip-send + error metric). The surrounding code already models graceful degradation for every other failure mode in this file (network errors return `(false, false)`, unconfigured providers early-return with a warn), so panicking on client construction is the odd path out.
Fix: propagate the build error (return a constructor `Result` / mark the provider unconfigured and log) so a TLS/cert init failure disables push fanout instead of crashing the worker.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/oauth.rs:920-931 — `verify_pkce` compares the recomputed S256 challenge to the stored `challenge` with the standard `==` operator (`computed == challenge`, line 927), which short-circuits and is not constant-time.

Practical exploitability is low: the compared value is the base64url of a SHA-256 digest bound to a single-use authorization code, so a timing side-channel does not yield a usable forgery (it would require a SHA-256 preimage, not a byte-by-byte guess). This is a defense-in-depth / hardening nit, not an active auth-bypass — noted at +1 for consistency with the rest of the OAuth path, which is otherwise well-hardened (PKCE required for all clients, argon2 constant-time client-secret verify, scope re-validation on issuance).
Fix (optional): use a constant-time comparison (e.g. `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` on equal-length byte slices) for the challenge match to keep the crypto-comparison surface uniform. Low priority.
